title: KlimaNot – Effects of climate change on geriatric patients in emergency and acute care
summary:
The study aims to investigate the potential influence of climate-change induced weather events on utilization of emergency departments and the spectrum of diseases treated there. Geriatric patients are focussed due to their known vulnerability to e.g. thermal conditions such as heat or cold. 
For this purpose, a prospective study will be conducted at three different geriatric clinics with an observation period of 12 months. To investigate the potential association of weather events and health condition in oldest-old patients, we analyze routine data of the hospital treatment as well as data from questionnaires. Additional insights linked to optimization in ambulatory care, prevention and hospital ressources shall also be derived from the findings of the study.
conditions: geriatric syndromes potentially associated to weather conditions

interventions.name:
oldest-olds with emergency admission to inpatient geriatric treatment undergoing:
- Baseline visit at study inclusion with collection of sociodemographic data (e.g., age, sex, level of care dependency), survey on individual perception of weather changes and home environment (study-specific question

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
non-scheduled hospital admission to geriatric ward via emergency department
Exclusion criteria:
age <85 years; final stage of acute/chronic disease (palliative care); secondary admission to geriatric department (not directly admitted from emergency department)
